To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The IVS+39C>T and IVS+181G>A variants in the resistins gene are associated with overfeeding induced changes in body composition, glucose tolerance and respiratory quotient.

the IVS2 + 39C>T polymorphisms were associated with overfeeding induced changes in abdominal visceral adipose tissue and the IVS2 +181G>A polymorphisms were related to changes in respiratory quotient.
the IVS2 + 181G>A variant of resistin was associated with changes in respiratory quotient in response to overeating.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of resistine gene polymorphisms on the response to a 4-month positive energy balance in 12 pairs of male twins.
the study of the genetic and molecular mechanisms that regulate the development of obesity and its complications.
the role of resistine in human metabolism and obesity, and its possible role as an adipokine in the regulation of glucose and fat metabolism.

these variants are associated with the changes induced in the body composition and metabolic parameters after overfeeding.

the IVS2 polymorphism is associated with the metabolic adaptation to positive energy balance and the IVS1 polymorphism with fat distribution.
